**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity).**

- **Clause:** § 7.2 (first of the two clauses numbered 7.2) — "Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives."
- **Why it fails:** It is a de facto exclusivity / right of first refusal binding us — no product-category limit, no 12-month cap, and no automatic termination on Cobalt's service-level or delivery failures. That misses the fallback entirely and lands in walk-away territory. It also contradicts § 12.3, where Cobalt acknowledges we have made no exclusivity or MFN commitment.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** delete the clause, reaching the preferred position, with a fallback offer of a category-limited, 12-month notice right terminable on SLA failure. Exclusivity running in our favour (§ 12.3) is left intact; the MFN dimension is left to the MFN rule.
